document: Federal Reserve Annual Report 2023 (Sample excerpt, 31 pages)

tree.title: Document Root
tree.description: The Federal Reserve's 2023 Annual Report covering monetary policy decisions, financial stability monitoring, and international cooperation throughout the year.

nodes.title: Monetary Policy
nodes.summary: The Federal Reserve continued its rate-tightening cycle in 2023, raising the federal funds rate target to a range of 5.25-5.50%. The committee balanced inflation control against the risk of excessive economic slowdown.

nodes.title: Overview of Monetary Policy Actions
nodes.summary: The FOMC raised rates four times in 2023 for a cumulative 100 basis points, while signaling a pause as inflation began trending toward the 2% target.

nodes.title: Economic Conditions
nodes.summary: GDP growth remained resilient at 2.5% for the year. Unemployment stayed near historic lows despite higher borrowing costs. Core PCE inflation declined from 4.9% to 3.2% over the course of the year.

nodes.title: Financial Stability
nodes.summary: The Federal Reserve monitored financial vulnerabilities including commercial real estate stress, bank funding conditions following the spring 2023 regional bank failures, and elevated asset valuations.

nodes.title: Monitoring Financial Vulnerabilities
nodes.summary: The Fed identified elevated CRE exposure among regional banks, tight funding conditions in the wake of the SVB collapse, and persistent but declining hedge fund leverage as key vulnerabilities.

nodes.title: Domestic and International Cooperation
nodes.summary: The Federal Reserve coordinated with the FDIC and OCC on domestic supervisory matters and engaged the FSB and BIS on cross-border regulatory alignment for systemically important institutions.

nodes.title: Federal Reserve Operations
nodes.summary: Balance sheet runoff continued at a pace of $60 billion per month for Treasuries and $35 billion for agency MBS. Total assets declined from $8.9 trillion to $7.7 trillion over the year.
